annotations.text:
Start here — this artboard is live.

The list is read-only state: one row per method, the same row the Settings page already uses for its switches, with a state chip and exactly one action. No row holds an input. Add and Manage open the one sheet to the right. Toggle Keyed off to see a guest vault: every second step says it needs a key first, and Add walks through both. Toggle Identity off: email and text codes say what they need instead of pretending.

One ceremony, every method.

The side sheet the Connectivity bar already opens, the card CeremonyShell already draws — what is being added, its facts, the fields, the one action inside the card — and the other keys as alternatives under the rule. Picking an alternative swaps the card; it never opens a second form. Try it: type a PIN, then switch to a password.

Verify before commit, then recovery codes.

Key (only when the vault has none), scan, confirm. The seed is written only once a live code matches — type 000 000 to see the refusal — and the recovery codes are shown once, right there, the step every reference product makes mandatory.

Email and text are fallbacks, and say so.

NIST 800-63B calls PSTN codes restricted and rules email out for out-of-band; the products that keep them put them last with a notice. The address is offered from the account (a FieldShell fill), the Identity API sends the code, and the vault key never leaves the device.

Unlock states who and which key.

The account row above both tabs, tabs for exactly the enrolled keys, and the second step announced before the first is taken. Step 2 (next artboard) offers exactly the second steps this vault enrolled, in the same tab vocabulary, with a recovery code as the way out.

The whole flow on one page.

Two ledgers: who (the account) and key (the vault). Each has its own exit. The unlock screen states both, and neither is ever allowed to stand in for the other.
